title: Reduction of finite etale lifting over a henselian pair to Noetherian henselian G-ring pairs
statement: Assume (H): for every henselian pair $(B,J)$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] with $B$ a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (in particular Noetherian), every proper morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] and every finite etale $Z_0$-scheme $W\to Z_0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], where $Z_0=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B}\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]), there are a finite etale $Z$-scheme $U'\to Z$ and an isomorphism of $Z_0$-schemes $U'\times_ZZ_0\cong W$ ((H) is the statement of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting-approximation]). Let $(A,I)$ be any henselian pair, $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism, $Y_0=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ its closed fibre, and $V\to Y_0$ a finite etale $Y_0$-scheme. Then there are a finite etale $Y$-scheme $U\to Y$ and an isomorphism of $Y_0$-schemes $U\times_YY_0\cong V$. (That is: essential surjectivity of $\mathsf{FEt}(Y)\to\mathsf{FEt}(Y_0)$ over all henselian pairs follows from the case of henselian pairs whose ring is a Noetherian G-ring.)

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma Tag 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), proof, paragraph 'General case', essential surjectivity (Limits 0A0P, More on Algebra 07PX, 0A04, 0AH3, Limits 01ZM, 01ZO, 07RP)

proof.text: Noetherian approximation of $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $f$ is proper. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-limit-noetherian] (affine clause) there are a directed set $\Lambda$ and an inverse system $(f_\lambda:Y_\lambda\to S_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ with affine transition morphisms, $f_\lambda$ proper, $S_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}A_\lambda$ with $A_\lambda$ a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra, $Y=\varprojlim_\lambda Y_\lambda$ (projections $p_\lambda:Y\to Y_\lambda$), $\operatorname{Spec}A=\varprojlim_\lambda S_\lambda$ and $A=\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda$ with coprojections $\alpha_\lambda:A_\lambda\to A$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], and $f_\lambda\circ p_\lambda=(\operatorname{Spec}\alpha_\lambda)\circ f$.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma Tag 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'General case' (lines ~1846-1878)

proof.text: The ideals. Put $I_\lambda=\alpha_\lambda^{-1}(I)\subseteq A_\lambda$. For $\mu\le\lambda$ the transition map $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}:A_\mu\to A_\lambda$ satisfies $\alpha_\lambda\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=\alpha_\mu$, so $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}(I_\mu)\subseteq I_\lambda$ and $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$ is a directed system of pairs. Every $x\in A$ is $\alpha_\lambda(a)$ for some $\lambda$ and $a\in A_\lambda$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]; if $x\in I$ then $a\in I_\lambda$. Hence $I=\bigcup_\lambda\alpha_\lambda(I_\lambda)$, i.e. $(A,I)=\varinjlim_\lambda(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$ as pairs, and the induced maps $A_\lambda/I_\lambda\to A/I$ are injective with union $A/I$, so $A/I=\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda/I_\lambda$. (Stacks: 'Thus we also have $I=\colim I_i$ and $A/I=\colim A_i/I_i$'.)

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma Tag 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'General case' (lines ~1846-1878)

proof.text: The closed fibres form an inverse system with limit $Y_0$. Put $S_{\lambda,0}=\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda/I_\lambda)$, $Y_{\lambda,0}=Y_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}S_{\lambda,0}$ and $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. (a) By step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], $S_0=\varprojlim_\lambda S_{\lambda,0}$. (b) For $\mu\le\lambda$ the morphism $Y_{\lambda,0}\to Y_{\mu,0}$ induced by $Y_\lambda\to Y_\mu$ and $S_{\lambda,0}\to S_{\mu,0}$ factors as $Y_{\lambda,0}=Y_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda/I_\lambda)\to Y_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda/I_\mu A_\lambda)=Y_\lambda\times_{Y_\mu}Y_{\mu,0}\to Y_{\mu,0}$: the first arrow is a base change of the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda/I_\lambda)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda/I_\mu A_\lambda)$ ($I_\mu A_\lambda\subseteq I_\lambda$ by step 2), hence a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], hence affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; the second is a base change of the affine $Y_\lambda\to Y_\mu$, hence affine [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]; a composite of affine morphisms is affine (preimages of affine opens stay affine). So $(Y_{\lambda,0})$ is an inverse system with affine transition morphisms, and its limit exists [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. (c) Each $Y_{\lambda,0}\to S_{\lambda,0}$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence quasi-compact and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]; as $S_{\lambda,0}$ is affine, $Y_{\lambda,0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. (d) $Y_0=\varprojlim_\lambda Y_{\lambda,0}$ with projections $q_\lambda=p_\lambda\times(S_0\to S_{\lambda,0}):Y_0\to Y_{\lambda,0}$: for every scheme $T$, $\operatorname{Mor}(T,\varprojlim Y_{\lambda,0})=\varprojlim_\lambda\big(\operatorname{Mor}(T,Y_\lambda)\times_{\operatorname{Mor}(T,S_\lambda)}\operatorname{Mor}(T,S_{\lambda,0})\big)$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and since limits commute with limits this is $\operatorname{Mor}(T,Y)\times_{\operatorname{Mor}(T,\operatorname{Spec}A)}\operatorname{Mor}(T,S_0)=\operatorname{Mor}(T,Y_0)$ by step 1 and (a), naturally in $T$; conclude by Yoneda. (Stacks: 'The same thing is true for schemes finite etale over $X_0=\lim(X_i\times_{S_i}S_{i,0})$'.)

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma Tag 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'General case' (lines ~1846-1878)

proof.text: Descent of $V$ to a finite stage. $V\to Y_0$ is finite, hence affine, quasi-compact and separated [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and etale, hence locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; so it is of finite presentation. By [thm-pd-spreading-out] (1), applied to the system $(Y_{\lambda,0})$ of step 3 (qcqs, affine transitions, limit $Y_0$), there are $\lambda_0$ and a morphism of finite presentation $V_{\lambda_0}\to Y_{\lambda_0,0}$ with $V_{\lambda_0}\times_{Y_{\lambda_0,0}}Y_0\cong V$ over $Y_0$; $V_{\lambda_0}$ is qcqs, being of finite presentation over the qcqs $Y_{\lambda_0,0}$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. For $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$ put $V_\lambda=V_{\lambda_0}\times_{Y_{\lambda_0,0}}Y_{\lambda,0}$: $V_\lambda\to Y_{\lambda,0}$ is the base change of $V_{\lambda_0}\to Y_{\lambda_0,0}$ to the stage $Y_{\lambda,0}$, and its base change to the limit $Y_0$ is $V\to Y_0$, finite and etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite] ($V_{\lambda_0}\to Y_{\lambda_0,0}$ locally of finite type) and [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale] (it is locally of finite presentation) there are $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge\lambda_0$ with $V_{\lambda_1}\to Y_{\lambda_1,0}$ finite and $V_{\lambda_2}\to Y_{\lambda_2,0}$ etale; for $\lambda\ge\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ ($\Lambda$ directed), $V_\lambda\to Y_{\lambda,0}$ is a base change of both, hence finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], and $V_\lambda\times_{Y_{\lambda,0}}Y_0\cong V$ over $Y_0$. Fix such a $\lambda$ from now on. (Stacks: the category of finite etale schemes over $X_0$ is the limit of those over the $X_{i,0}$, by Limits 01ZM, 01ZO, 07RP; only its essential surjectivity is used here.)

proof.text: The henselization of the stage. Let $(A_\lambda^h,I_\lambda^h)$, $I^h_\lambda=I_\lambda A^h_\lambda$, be the henselization of $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], with $\eta:A_\lambda\to A_\lambda^h$. Then: (i) $(A_\lambda^h,I_\lambda^h)$ is a henselian pair and $A_\lambda/I_\lambda\to A_\lambda^h/I_\lambda^h$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] (2),(3); (ii) $A_\lambda$ is a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra, hence a G-ring [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-z-g-ring], so $A^h_\lambda$ is a G-ring, in particular Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-pair-g-ring]; (iii) as $(A,I)=\varinjlim(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$ (step 2) is henselian, there is a ring map $\beta:A_\lambda^h\to A$ with $\beta\eta=\alpha_\lambda$, mapping $I_\lambda^h$ into $I$ [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-colimit] (Stacks records more: $A=\varinjlim A_i^h$; only the map $\beta$ is used for essential surjectivity).

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma Tag 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'General case' (lines ~1846-1878)

proof.text: Lift at the stage by (H). Put $Y^h_\lambda=Y_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}\operatorname{Spec}A^h_\lambda$; it is proper over $\operatorname{Spec}A^h_\lambda$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Its closed fibre is $Y^h_\lambda\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A^h_\lambda}\operatorname{Spec}(A^h_\lambda/I^h_\lambda)=Y_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}\operatorname{Spec}(A^h_\lambda/I^h_\lambda)$ (associativity of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]), and the $S_\lambda$-isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A^h_\lambda/I^h_\lambda)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda/I_\lambda)=S_{\lambda,0}$ of step 5 (i) identifies it with $Y_{\lambda,0}$; let $j:Y_{\lambda,0}\to Y^h_\lambda$ be the resulting morphism, with components $Y_{\lambda,0}\to Y_\lambda$ and $Y_{\lambda,0}\to S_{\lambda,0}\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_\lambda^h/I_\lambda^h)\to\operatorname{Spec}A^h_\lambda$. By step 5, $(A^h_\lambda,I^h_\lambda)$ is a henselian pair with $A^h_\lambda$ a G-ring, so (H), applied to $B=A^h_\lambda$, $J=I^h_\lambda$, $Z=Y^h_\lambda$ and the finite etale $V_\lambda\to Y_{\lambda,0}$ of step 4, gives a finite etale $U_\lambda\to Y^h_\lambda$ with $U_\lambda\times_{Y^h_\lambda,j}Y_{\lambda,0}\cong V_\lambda$ over $Y_{\lambda,0}$. (Stacks: 'we formally deduce the result for $X/\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ from the result for the $(X_i\times_{S_i}\operatorname{Spec}(A_i^h))/\operatorname{Spec}(A_i^h)$'.)

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma Tag 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'General case' (lines ~1846-1878)

proof.text: Base change to $Y$. The morphisms $p_\lambda:Y\to Y_\lambda$ and $Y\xrightarrow{f}\operatorname{Spec}A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}\beta}\operatorname{Spec}A^h_\lambda$ agree over $S_\lambda$: $f_\lambda p_\lambda=(\operatorname{Spec}\alpha_\lambda)f$ (step 1) and $\operatorname{Spec}\eta\circ\operatorname{Spec}\beta=\operatorname{Spec}(\beta\eta)=\operatorname{Spec}\alpha_\lambda$ (step 5). So they define $g:Y\to Y^h_\lambda$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $U=U_\lambda\times_{Y^h_\lambda,g}Y$; as a base change of the finite etale $U_\lambda\to Y^h_\lambda$, $U\to Y$ is finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category].

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma Tag 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'General case' (lines ~1846-1878)

proof.text: The closed fibre of $U$. Let $i:Y_0\to Y$ be the projection and $q_\lambda:Y_0\to Y_{\lambda,0}$ the projection of step 3 (d). Then $g\circ i=j\circ q_\lambda$: the components in $Y_\lambda$ are both $p_\lambda\circ i$; the components in $\operatorname{Spec}A^h_\lambda$ are both $Y_0\to S_0\to\operatorname{Spec}A^h_\lambda$, given by ring maps $A^h_\lambda\to A/I$, namely $A^h_\lambda\xrightarrow{\beta}A\to A/I$ and $A^h_\lambda\to A^h_\lambda/I^h_\lambda\cong A_\lambda/I_\lambda\to A/I$; both kill $I^h_\lambda$ (step 5 (iii)), and the induced maps $A^h_\lambda/I^h_\lambda\to A/I$ agree after precomposition with the isomorphism $A_\lambda/I_\lambda\to A^h_\lambda/I^h_\lambda$ induced by $\eta$, where both give the map induced by $\alpha_\lambda$ ($\beta\eta=\alpha_\lambda$); hence they are equal. Therefore, pasting cartesian squares [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting], $U\times_YY_0=U_\lambda\times_{Y^h_\lambda,gi}Y_0=U_\lambda\times_{Y^h_\lambda,jq_\lambda}Y_0\cong(U_\lambda\times_{Y^h_\lambda,j}Y_{\lambda,0})\times_{Y_{\lambda,0}}Y_0\cong V_\lambda\times_{Y_{\lambda,0}}Y_0\cong V$, all isomorphisms over $Y_0$ (steps 6 and 4). So $U$ is a finite etale $Y$-scheme with $U\times_YY_0\cong V$ as $Y_0$-schemes.

split_report.summary: Rewrote the statement (it was an instruction) as the reduction of finite etale lifting over an arbitrary henselian pair to the case of henselian pairs with a Noetherian G-ring, with that case as explicit hypothesis (H) = statement of lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting-approximation; dropped the claim on isomorphisms/full faithfulness, which no user needs (the parent's step 2 uses only essential surjectivity). Proof in 8 steps following pione.tex 0GS2 'General case': Noetherian approximation (Limits 0A0P, new node lem-weil-pbc-proper-limit-noetherian with the affine clause Stacks uses), the ideals I_i = preimages (elementary), the closed fibres Y_{i,0} as an inverse system with limit Y_0 (written out: affine transitions, qcqs, Yoneda), descent of V to a finite etale V_i (thm-pd-spreading-out tool use, descend-finite 01ZO, descend-etale 07RP), henselization of the stage (pair-henselization 0A02, new nodes lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-z-g-ring 07PX, lem-weil-pbc-henselization-pair-g-ring 0AH3, lem-weil-pbc-henselization-colimit 0A04 for the map A_i^h -> A), application of (H) to Y_i x_{S_i} Spec A_i^h, base change to Y and identification of the closed fibre by pasting. Stacks' 'A = colim A_i^h' and the limit-of-categories phrasing are only needed for full faithfulness; the essential-surjectivity argument uses the single map A_i^h -> A. Mathlib: no G-rings, no henselization (HenselianRing class only), no Noetherian approximation of proper morphisms; three kinds of search recorded on every new node.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finiteEtale_lift_of_henselianPair_of_gRing_lifting (H : ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B], IsGRing B → ∀ (J : Ideal B) [HenselianRing B J] (Z : Scheme.{u}) (g : Z ⟶ Spec (.of B)) [IsProper g] (W : (@IsFinite ⊓ @Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).Over ⊤ (pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J))))), ∃ U' : (@IsFinite ⊓ @Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).Over ⊤ Z, Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.snd U'.hom (pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J))))) ≅ Over.mk W.hom)) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [HenselianRing A I] {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f] (V : (@IsFinite ⊓ @Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).Over ⊤ (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))))) : ∃ U : (@IsFinite ⊓ @Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).Over ⊤ Y, Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.snd U.hom (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))))) ≅ Over.mk V.hom)
